vr.look: An exhibit is a display that teaches visitors. A strong exhibit has four parts: a map, a source (something real from the past), a community connection, and a virtue.

models.name: Quill Brown
models.why: Source: people wrote things down long ago

steps.title: Get ready
steps.html:
These are the models you will use. In VR, type the gray word in the Models search box to find each one.

@MODELS@

In VR, this page is on the Canvas tab too.

steps.title: Go in
steps.html:
🔗 First time only: connect Canvas at xr.optimaed.com. See Having trouble in VR? below.

Open the On-Demand app. Click Explore. Type Gallery in Filter environments. Click Optima Gallery, then Begin Solo.

steps.title: Build the exhibit
steps.html:
Find an open wall or corner in the gallery. Make 4 spots in a row: map, source, community, virtue.

Put the globe and compass rose in the map spot, the quill in the source spot, the house in the community spot, and the Courage book in the virtue spot.

steps.title: Take your photo and send it
steps.html:
Open your menu, click Library, then Camera. Move the tablet until your whole diorama fits. Click Take photo.

Click the Canvas tab and pick @CANVAS@. Click Choose from My Files, pick your photo, click Use this file, then Submit to Canvas. Look for the green Submitted tag.

🔁 Want to fix it? Take a new photo and send it again.

steps.title: Check and leave
steps.html: Press the Meta button, then click Quit. Check that your photo is in the Canvas assignment. Not there? Open Having trouble in VR?

extra.html: Make every model big enough for a visitor to see from far away.

vr.full: One photo that shows all four parts of your exhibit.

studio.title: Build the Exhibit Panel
studio.look: An empty exhibit panel with four frames: Map, Source, Community and Virtue. For each frame, you get three choices. Only one is clear and true for a visitor.
studio.do: Read the question. Tap the strongest choice for that frame.

game.done: Your panel is complete! A map, a source, a community and a virtue, all easy for a visitor to read.

parts.name: Map
parts.q: Which map label helps a visitor most?

choices.text: Florida is in the Southeast region, on a peninsula between the Gulf and the Atlantic.
choices.why: Yes! It names the region and the place clearly.

choices.text: Florida is the best state in the world.
choices.why: That is an opinion, not a map fact.

parts.name: Source
parts.q: Which source label tells the truth?

choices.text: A real photo I made up the date for.
choices.why: Honesty: never make up a date.

choices.text: Page 1 of the U.S. Constitution, 1787, National Archives.
choices.why: Yes! It says what it is, when, and where it comes from.
Too vague. What is it, and when?

parts.name: Community
parts.q: Which line connects the exhibit to a real community?

choices.why: That does not tell a visitor anything.
That is not true, and not kind.

choices.text: In my town, people trade at the market and vote at the library.
choices.why: Yes! It shows real people doing real things.

parts.name: Virtue
parts.q: Which line shows a virtue in action?

choices.text: Courage: Frederick Douglass spoke for freedom, even when it was dangerous.
choices.why: Yes! It names a virtue and shows a real person living it.
Which virtue? Show it in action.
Courage means doing right even when you are scared.

frames.lead: Which part of your exhibit is strongest?
frames.starter: The strongest part of my exhibit is ...
I want a visitor to learn ...

studio.full: All four frames are filled, and your 2 sentences have 20 words or more.
